newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to probe $1.4 bln Raytheon contract.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to probe $1.4 bln Raytheon contract.

text.p: The Brazilian government's financial watchdog has asked public prosecutors to probe a $1.4 billion contract awarded to U.S. high-technology giant Raytheon Co for an Amazonian radar surveillance system, a spokesman said.
Spokesman Marcos Santos said the Federal Accounts Tribunal (TCU) had requested the investigation because it needed more information on the project before ruling on a complaint brought by a senator.
"The TCU decided it needed a deeper investigation before it could evaluate the case," Santos said.

Senator Antonio Carlos Valadares has alleged that Raytheon plans to set up only half the number of radar stations originally agreed for the surveillance system and that their unit costs had been considerably increased.
No one was immediately available for comment in Raytheon's Brazil headquarters located in Rio de Janeiro's Sheraton hotel.

Known by its Portuguese acronym Sivam, the project combines air and ground-based radar to allow Brazil to monitor environmental destruction and drugs and contraband smuggling in the vast expanse of the Amazon river basin.
The project was dependent on financing by the U.S. Eximbank, which was finally approved by the Brazilian Senate last year after months of wrangling and criticism at the cost.
